solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make millions bringing in British editor for big title

indicators.note: the make-millions pair takes the British editor letters into its middle

parts.note: to make something is to do it
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A newspaper owner gets rich by hiring a British editor and is rewarded with a peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dukedom is the highest rank of the British peerage, so it is a grand hereditary rank.

clue.text: Shower for marcher

definitions.meaning: read as 'one who shows', a person who displays how something works
someone who walks in a protest march

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between a bathroom fitting and a protester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' wants to be the bathroom kind or rain; here it is one who shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person giving a demonstration of a product and a street protester are called by this word.

clue.text: Cambridge college's joint ruling position

parts.note: King's is a famous Cambridge college, with its possessive S
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A shared seat of authority belonging to a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like 'shared' but is the body part HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or status of a monarch is the position of one who rules.

clue.text: State of mind upset, getting judgment

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mood is a state of mind

explanation.surface: Someone feeling upset receives a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal or a feeling, but in a down light it turns MOOD over.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom in the old sense is a sentence or verdict, as in the Day of Judgment, Doomsday.

clue.text: Chap put up paintings as aid to meditation

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: in a down light, put up means raised, so the word for paintings is read upwards

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A man hangs pictures to help himself meditate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like hanging pictures; it turns ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or sound repeated to focus the mind while meditating.

clue.text: Introductory statement before walk

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
to amble is to walk in a leisurely way

explanation.surface: Someone makes a few opening remarks before setting off on a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is a preliminary passage or opening remark that leads into the main text.

clue.text: Ruin what one's cooking

definitions.meaning: to ... someone's hopes is to wreck them, informal
a prepared food item being made in the kitchen

explanation.surface: A cook ruining the meal they are making.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally one can spoil chances this way, and a prepared course of food goes by the same word.

clue.text: Greeting that's lippy, not touching

parts.note: a salutation made with puckered lips that never meet the cheek; 'lippy' usually means cheeky or insolent

explanation.surface: An insolent hello from someone keeping their distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lippy' suggests a cheeky greeting; it literally means done with the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a pretend kiss given near the cheek without contact, a social gesture of greeting.

clue.text: Regular fighters not yet knocked down?

definitions.meaning: a permanent professional force of soldiers maintained in peacetime
taken literally, a fighting force still on its feet and upright

explanation.surface: Professional boxers still on their feet after a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second reading as playful: an army that is still upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent force of professional soldiers, kept even in peacetime, is the regular military.

clue.text: Weekend nearly over, heavy rain

parts.note: when the weekend is over it is Monday, abbreviated MON
something nearly over will happen soon, i.e. Monday comes soon

explanation.surface: Sunday evening gloom as the weekend ends in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first three words as 'Monday soon': with the weekend nearly over, MON comes SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal wind of South Asia brings torrential downpours, and the word is used for that rainy season.

clue.text: Body part extra cheap if not complete

indicators.note: the phrase is used incompletely, with its first two letters and its last letter dropped, leaving a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: An organ on offer at a bargain price, provided it is missing bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if not complete' asks for part of 'extra cheap', losing EX and P.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the tube carrying air from the throat to the lungs, an anatomical part.

clue.text: Inside a larger one, fit snug retreat

definitions.text: Inside a larger one, fit snug
definitions.meaning: to fit tightly within a bigger one, as stacking tables or Russian dolls do
a cosy, secluded place to withdraw to, a den or haven

explanation.surface: A cosy bolt-hole that fits snugly inside a bigger house.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacking things one within another is the verb; a bird's home or a snug den is the noun.

clue.text: Astronomical council is right

parts.note: star used as an adjective, belonging to astronomy
a board is a governing council or committee

explanation.surface: A committee of astronomers is correct in its findings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is the side of a ship, not 'correct'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, this is the right-hand side when facing forward, opposite to port.

clue.text: Strange moves, introducing European officer

indicators.note: the European letter is brought into the middle of the rearranged letters
the letters of the word strange are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Odd behaviour as a European officer is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges STRANGE as SERGANT; 'introducing' slips E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer in the army or a police rank is a sergeant.

clue.text: Old family member losing head jigs on peak

indicators.note: the dances word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: jigs are lively folk dances
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A dancing great-grandparent loses their head while jigging on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the D of DANCES to give ANCES; TOR is a rocky peak in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear from earlier generations is a relative from the family's past.

clue.text: Concerned with teaching story that can be put right

parts.note: re means about or regarding
a parable is a simple story told to teach a moral lesson

explanation.surface: A moral tale about how damage can be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repairable can be mended, so it is able to be fixed.

clue.text: Old phone beginning to break down

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word break is taken

parts.note: lower means further down

explanation.surface: An old telephone that starts to break down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like part of 'break down' but means LOWER; the blower is dated British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned British slang for the telephone, as in 'get on the blower'.

clue.text: Quantity of work by British composer

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work or energy in physics

explanation.surface: A body of compositions by a British composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' seems to credit a writer, but just places B beside ERG; Alban Berg was an Austrian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, who wrote the opera Wozzeck.

clue.text: Weapon trooped about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters of trooped are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers marched around carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile fired from submarines or ships is an armament.

clue.text: Needing some prompting to play boisterously

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word prompting is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Children need encouragement to play rough games.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to frolic in a lively, noisy, rough way, as children do.

clue.text: Gallery of idols?

definitions.meaning: the highest balcony in a theatre, with the cheapest seats

explanation.surface: A museum room full of graven images.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British theatre the gods is the top gallery, far from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost theatre balcony and worshipped deities both go by this word.

clue.text: Way to interrupt one courting Bertie

indicators.note: the way abbreviation breaks into the middle of the suitor word

parts.note: a wooer is a suitor, someone courting
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A suitor is rudely interrupted while wooing someone called Bertie.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's comic upper-class hero, served by his valet Jeeves.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of Wodehouse's hapless gentleman narrator gives his surname.

clue.text: Love affair as African politicians enter European capital

indicators.note: the politicians go into the capital, so their letters sit inside it

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: An affair blossoms as South African politicians visit Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love relationship, especially a passionate or brief one.

clue.text: Prayers organised for work on car

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters of prayers are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Organised prayers offered for a car to be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Repainting a vehicle body is a job done in a garage to its paintwork.
